messages:
jamie: Heads-up — seeing a p99 spike on prod-serving-2 starting ~08:10 UTC. Correlates with requests that include long prompts (+ tool calls) and some outlier generations. KV cache lookups jumping, then we fall back to a slower kernel path. Can someone help triage?

infra-bot: alert: latency.p99(prod-serving-2) crossed 1.8s at 2026-03-16T08:10:12Z. top causes: long_prompt, tool_loop_retry.

alex: Can you paste the short perfreport you grabbed? Also which model variant + kernel plan?

jamie: quick dump below (trimmed). noticed "kernel_fallback: matmul_fp32" lines and a lot of `kv_cache_evict` spikes.

```
# perf-summary
requests: 2,340/s
p95: 420ms
p99: 1.92s
avg_memcpy_ms: 12.4
kernel_fallback_count: 87
kv_cache_evictions: 223
hot_kernels: matmul_fp32, attention_unfused
trace_hint: repeated_generate -> tool_call -> regenerate
```

maria: that trace_hint screams tool-calling loop. user flow: model emits tool_call, app calls external tool, tool returns, model re-enters generation with full original prefix appended -> prompt grows. If KV cache is per-request and keying includes prefixes, you lose cache reuse.

sandeep: yeah — we saw similar when prompt_length > ~8k tokens. Two things collide: (1) kernel selection heuristics prefer specialized int8/fast kernels for typical seq-lens, but a sudden long prompt forces a path that selects unfused attention kernels -> slower, (2) KV cache churn/eviction when replica batch mix includes short and very long contexts.

ryan: reproduction steps I ran locally: 1) synthetic tool-loop that appends last tool output to prompt every step 2) call with variety of batch sizes. Observed p99 grows superlinearly with microbatch_size >= 8 for mixed-length workloads.

alex: actionable checklist:
- collect perf trace for one impacted machine (runcore trace)
- try dynamic microbatch sizing (limit effective microbatch for long-context reqs)
- add short-circuit for tool-calls so they don't join normal batching
- prototype KV cache soft-eviction policy keyed by prefix fingerprint

jamie: attaching the collect command I used:
```
rtrace collect --node prod-serving-2 --pid 4882 --duration 120 --tags kernel,kv,queue
```

sandeep: initial idea for KV: track per-request fingerprint of prefix tokens; if a new incoming request's prefix fingerprint doesn't match any hot cache entry and prompt_len > threshold, mark it as "cold" and exclude from shared KV slab (put in ephemeral per-request allocation). That avoids thrashing the shared cache.

maria: +1. Also for batching: prefer policy where tool-calls are always 1) prioritized for low-latency path or 2) forced into a smaller microbatch cap (like cap=2). Throughput suffers slightly but p99 wins. We should codify this as a routing policy: route_by_latency_hint.

alex: kernel-selection tweak: if avg_prefix_len > X then bias kernel planner to choose fused-attention fallback even if it costs a tiny more memory, because the current fallback (matmul_fp32) is much worse. I'll sketch a patch to kernel planner to add a heuristic on seq_len_distribution.

ryan: small mitigation we rolled for a similar incident: detect repeated regen cycles (same trace_id re-entering generate > 3x within 30s) -> add a transient circuit-breaker that returns a truncated prompt or a canned fallback and alerts owner. prevents unbounded loops.

jamie: profiling snippet from one of the slow requests (stack samples, aggregated):
```
20% attention_unfused::forward
17% matmul_fp32::gemm
12% memcpy_device_to_device
9% kv_cache::lookup
8% scheduler::batching_wait
5% tool_invoke_http::send
```

maria: that scheduler::batching_wait at 9% is the microbatch queuing hitting outliers. If we cap microbatch growth per-route we can shave that. But we need guardrails so we don't blow up throughput for short contexts.

sandeep: tradeoff summary: increase microbatch => better throughput & p95, worse p99 for mixed workloads. Solution: dynamic microbatching keyed by route fingerprint + explicit latency SLO flag that bypasses batching when SLO strict.

alex: quick experiment plan (who/when):
- jamie: run rtrace collect across 3 nodes + upload traces (today)
- alex: patch kernel planner heuristic and run A/B (tomorrow)
- sandeep: prototype KV soft-evict policy in dev env (2 days)
- maria: add new alert rule for regen-loops + routing policy stub (today)

ryan: PR snippet for batching bypass (pseudo):
```
if (req.hints.contains("tool_calling") && req.prompt_len > 8000) {
  route.set_microbatch_cap(1);
  route.set_latency_priority(true);
}
```

jamie: thanks. I'll kick off traces now. If we confirm KV thrash + kernel fallback chain is root cause we can prioritize stopping the thrash first (evict policy) and then tune kernel planner.

alex: also add a short-run canary: deploy kernel heuristic to 10% traffic and run the same synthetic tool-loop load to ensure we don't regress throughput for normal flows.

maria: owning the alert and the routing policy spec. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:

infra-bot: action created: INCIDENT-2026-0316-77 assigned to maria, severity: P2, due: 2026-03-18.

jamie: will update thread with traces & results. thanks team :thumbsup:
